ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, Fuel Systems to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to own integration and test of the fuel system for Omen, an advanced Group 3 VTOL tail-sitting aircraft. This individual will own fuel system integration testing across increasingly mature environments, from component bench tests through full vehicle ground test, and will support the vehicle-level mass properties test program by defining and planning the fuel-system-specific inputs needed to account for the effects of fuel state and vehicle orientation on weight, center of gravity, and moments of inertia. This is a hands-on, build-and-run role suited to someone who wants to own a test campaign end to end: requirements, fixturing, execution, and reporting.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own all fuel system integration and test activities from component bench tests through full vehicle ground test, including tanks, pumps, valves, fluid lines, sensors, and dispense sequencing, developing right-sized test plans and efficiently capturing and reporting learnings as inputs to design
  • Define and plan the fuel-system-specific requirements, measurement approach, and instrumentation needed to characterize vehicle weight, center of gravity, and moments of inertia, supporting the vehicle mass properties test program across fuel states and vehicle orientations
  • Develop and execute a fuel system orientation test program capturing fuel flow behavior, pump performance, and tank dispense sequencing across multiple vehicle orientations
  • Define fixturing, tooling, and test setup requirements for fuel system bench and vehicle-level orientation testing, partnering with fabrication and ground support teams on buildup of long-lead hardware
  • Coordinate with structures/loads and systems engineering teams to define the load cases and vehicle configurations required to support orientation and mass properties testing
  • Feed mass properties test results into vehicle models and hand off clean data to support downstream ground vibration testing (GVT) and flight dynamics work
  • Focus on the safety of integration environments, ensuring that potential harm to team members is eliminated by design, with particular attention to fuel/hazardous fluid handling and heavy-lift or orientation-change operations
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of fuel system integration environments and test fixtures
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test of prototype and production representative systems

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical, Aerospace, Systems, or related engineering discipline
  • 5+ years experience in integration and test of fluid/fuel systems, and/or aircraft mass properties (weight and balance) test programs
  • Experience with aircraft or vehicle mass properties measurement techniques (e.g., weight and balance, moment of inertia measurement via pendulum/swing or similar methods) and associated instrumentation
  • Experience with fuel or fluid system components (tanks, pumps, valves, fluid lines, and associated sensors) and fluid system test setups
  • Experience defining fixturing and test setup requirements for fluid system rigs or multi-orientation ground testing
  • Adept at working safely with fuel, hazardous fluids, and pressurized systems
  • Strong test engineering foundation — DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, and fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial)
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal and written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with tail-sitter, VTOL, or unconventional aircraft configurations where fuel state and vehicle orientation significantly impact performance and mass properties.
  • Familiarity with autonomous air vehicle (AAV) or UAS integration environments, particularly Group 3 platforms operating in runway-independent or shipboard contexts.
  • Experience feeding test data into vehicle-level models for downstream analysis such as ground vibration testing (GVT) or flight dynamics characterization.
  • Exposure to production-representative test campaigns, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) processes and configuration control in a rapid-iteration hardware development environment.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team at Anduril develops operationally relevant, multi-asset autonomy. We are focused on new air vehicle development programs, and making large groups of autonomous systems work effectively together. Within the Maneuver Dominance team, we are growing an early-stage, undisclosed autonomous air vehicle (AAV) program at our Costa Mesa HQ. This team is chartered with re-inventing an existing platform through heavy modification and integration of advanced autonomy, mission systems, and payloads. On this team, you will be tackling novel challenges across airframe, structures, avionics, and software from day one. As part of this program, you'll work alongside a tight-knit group of mechanical, structural, electrical, and software engineers, together with Program Leads and the Chief Engineer, all embedded in a single team driving toward major milestones. You will work in a lean, high-ownership culture where the entire vehicle team sits side-by-side, iterating quickly and making decisions in real time. Given the early stage of the program, you will have influence over foundational architecture decisions and the opportunity to redefine an existing platform.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration and Test Engineer with a strong software focus to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to help develop and scale our Hardware-In-The-Loop (HITL) capabilities. This role will focus on the software infrastructure, test framework, automation, and tooling required to bring up and operate complex HITL systems. You will work at the intersection of simulation, hardware integration, and system-level testing to enable reliable and repeatable testing on physical systems.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop and maintain the test framework and software infrastructure that bridges our Software-In-The-Loop (SITL) testing to Hardware-In-The-Loop testing, enabling a seamless testing experience across both environments
  • Develop logging infrastructure and log-processing tooling to capture, organize, correlate, and analyze system behavior during HITL testing
  • Develop diagnostics and telemetry debug capabilities that provide visibility into system state and enable efficient troubleshooting of integration and test failures
  • Develop fault-injection capabilities that enable controlled failures and degraded conditions to be introduced and evaluated during testing
  • Build automated tests to evaluate system behavior, fault detection, handling, recovery, and graceful degradation
  • Develop configuration management tracking tools to maintain consistent and reproducible HITL configurations
  • Automate HITL health checks, setup, configuration, deployment, and test execution to reduce manual effort and improve repeatability
  • Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for regression testing
  • Establish software and testing best practices that enable HITL systems to be used as a reliable part of the development and integration lifecycle
  • Support the physical stand-up, configuration, and maintenance of open-loop and closed-loop HITLs, and the integration of hardware, compute, networking, sensors, and other components required for HITL testing
  • Troubleshoot and resolve real-time simulation issues during HITL operations, including timing constraints, hardware interface problems, and model fidelity discrepancies
  • Work closely with software, systems, simulation, and hardware engineers to identify and resolve integration and test issues
  • Act with a strong safety mindset (“Stop, Think, Do”) while operating in prototype and experimental environments with the aim of eliminating potential harm to team members.
  • Follow established procedures and identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, and efficiency

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

  • Bachelor’s Degree (or similar) in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace/Aeronautics Engineering, or similar
  • Ability to take ownership of software infrastructure from development through deployment, testing, and maintenance.
  • Experience developing automated test frameworks, CI/CD pipelines, configuration management processes, and test tooling such as logging, diagnostics, and debug utilities
  • Strong proficiency in Python and C++
  • Experience with Github
  • Experience developing, operating, and maintaining software frameworks for HIL/HITL/Ironbird/System Support Equipment for a Group 4 or Group 5 UAS, aerospace, or defense vehicle integration and test environment
  • Understanding of software/hardware interfaces, networking, and electrical bus protocols (CAN, Ethernet, RS-232/422/485, MIL-STD-1553)
  • Strong debugging skills and the ability to troubleshoot issues across software and hardware boundaries
  • Prior hands on experience working with and troubleshooting electrical systems, harnesses, LRUs, and electro-mechanical assemblies
  • Experience using diagnostic and protocol analysis tools such as Saleae Logic Analyzers, Wireshark, PEAK-System CAN interfaces, or similar tools
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and adapt quickly in a face-paced development environment
  • Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal and communication skills
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia desirable

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and engineering documentation
  • Experience performing LRU-, subsystem-, and system-level hardware integration and bring-up
  • Prior experience with oscilloscopes, digital multi-meters, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, and other electrical test equipment
  • Familiarity with Nix

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, specializing in Surrogate Testing to join the Omen team at our Costa Mesa HQ. Omen is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that packs the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger airplanes into a novel runway-independent Group 3 platform. Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. Omen is the first tail-sitter aircraft with a mass-production contract, with an order of 50 systems representing a decisive investment that anchors production and accelerates the development of future systems.

You will lead the planning, integration, and execution of flight test activities using surrogate platforms, including crewed test-beds with representative payload pods, full-size mock-ups, and powertrain rigs to characterize and demonstrate subsystem performance in representative environments before integration into air vehicles. All of this in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own surrogate platform test activities including crewed carry/representative pod configurations, full-size mock-ups (with partial or full system integration) and powertrain rigs
  • Develop, review, and execute right-sized test plans for surrogate flight test activities, efficiently capturing and reporting learnings, and making recommendations as inputs to design
  • Lead integration of Vehicle and Mission System components onto surrogate platforms for characterization in representative flight envelopes (altitude, airspeed, temperature, vibration)
  • Evolve and demonstrate Support System design with full-size mock-ups
  • Coordinate crewed surrogate operations including pod integration, instrumentation, pre-flight checks, and mission planning
  • Support subscale UAS flight operations for software and subsystem development teams
  • Plan and execute powertrain rig operations for powertrain and control system integration testing
  • Ensure safety of airborne test environments through structured hazard identification and risk management
  • Coordinate test range access, airspace approvals, spectrum approvals, and operational permissions across CONUS and UAE locations
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of surrogate test assets and installed instrumentation
  • Support Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) integration, including telemetry systems, for real-time data during surrogate flights

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor degree or higher in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering or aviation related technical discipline
  • 5+ years experience in flight test operations, preferably with uncrewed or autonomous air systems (Group 3 or larger)
  • Experience integrating subsystems, payloads, and flight test instrumentation (FTI) onto flight platforms, including telemetry and real-time monitoring
  • Knowledge of airspace management, flight test safety and test range operations
  • Adept at working safely with high voltage systems, including integration, checkout and test
  • Strong test engineering foundation — DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial), and command line interface (CLI)
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal and written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with surrogate or test-bed aircraft operations, including crewed platforms carrying representative payload pods or instrumented mock-ups for subsystem characterization prior to integration onto target vehicles.
  • Familiarity with tail-sitter, VTOL, or unconventional aircraft configurations and the unique flight test considerations they introduce, such as orientation-dependent system behavior and transition-phase testing.
  • Experience coordinating test range access, airspace approvals, and spectrum authorizations across multiple sites, including OCONUS locations.
  • Background in subscale UAS flight operations supporting rapid software and subsystem development cycles, with an emphasis on feeding test results directly back into design iteration

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking an Integration & Test Engineer, Electrical Systems to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to own integration and test of electrical systems for Omen, an advanced Group 3 VTOL tail-sitting aircraft. This individual will own integration and test activities across electrical systems including avionics, power systems, actuator and motor controls, mission systems, networking, sensors, and harnessing. This is a hands-on, build-and-run role suited to someone who wants to own a test campaign end to end: requirements, tooling, execution, and reporting.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support bring-up, functional checkout, and troubleshooting of electrical hardware across multiple vehicle systems
  • Develop and execute right-sized test plans and procedures for electrical component and subsystem integration
  • Coordinate with design engineers across disciplines (electrical, GNC, mission systems, flight software) to burn-down design risks and demonstrate system maturity
  • Use standard electrical test instrumentation (multimeter, oscilloscope, logic analyzer, spectrum and network analyzer) to characterize hardware and diagnose failures
  • Write and maintain test scripts and tooling (Python or similar) to automate data capture, sequencing, and reporting
  • Follow and maintain safety protocols for high voltage and stored energy hazards during integration and test activities
  • Maintain configuration control records for test hardware, tooling, and firmware/software versions
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test activities for prototype and production representative system

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or related engineering discipline
  • 1+ years of experience in integration and test, electrical hardware bring-up, or embedded systems/firmware work with hands-on hardware validation
  • Demonstrated hands-on proficiency with multimeters, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers
  • Working software/firmware literacy (C, Python, or similar) sufficient to read embedded code, write test scripts, and reason through firmware behavior during hardware debug
  • Comfort working across more than one electrical domain (power electronics, controls, communications)
  • Fluency in at least one common communication protocol (CAN, Ethernet, or Serial)
  • Willingness and demonstrated aptitude to work safely with high voltage systems (400V+) under supervision
  • Basic EMI/EMC fluency (conducted/radiated susceptibility or emissions)
  • Wiring harness design, sizing, or fabrication experience
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, with clear verbal and written communication skills
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense industry background not required, but genuine interest in the mission is
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australia

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with electrical system integration on aerospace or UAS platforms, particularly involving avionics, actuator controls, and power distribution in space-constrained, weight-sensitive environments.
  • Familiarity with EMI/EMC testing and mitigation techniques in integrated vehicle environments, including conducted and radiated emissions troubleshooting on densely packaged systems.
  • Experience automating test workflows end to end — from data acquisition and sequencing through automated report generation — using Python or similar scripting languages.
  • Exposure to VTOL, tail-sitter, or unconventional aircraft architectures where electrical system behavior varies significantly across flight modes and vehicle orientations

You will plan and execute Powertrain integration and test activities across increasingly mature environments, from discrete bench tests through Hardware In Lab (HIL), Hardware In The Loop (HITL), surrogate platforms, and flight test. The Powertrain scope encompasses electric machines, inverters, gearboxes, battery modules, battery management systems (BMS), high voltage distribution, powertrain controllers, power conditioning, and associated thermal management systems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will own component and subsystem test campaigns end to end and contribute to vehicle-level campaigns led by senior engineering. All of this in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Plan and execute powertrain (propulsion drive, battery, hybrid management) test activities across increasingly mature integration environments, owning individual test campaigns end to end
  • Develop, review, and execute right-sized test plans for Powertrain component and subsystem integration, efficiently capturing and reporting learnings, and making recommendations as inputs to design
  • Perform integration, bring-up, and characterization of electric machines, inverters, gearboxes, battery modules, BMS, high voltage distribution, powertrain controllers, and power conditioning components
  • Support development and operation of the Powertrain surrogate for integrated powertrain characterization and control tuning
  • Focus on the safety of integration environments, ensuring that potential harm to team members is eliminated by design, with particular attention to high voltage and stored energy hazards
  • Implement and maintain processes for configuration control of Powertrain integration environments
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), ground test, and flight test of prototype and production representative systems

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor degree or higher in Electrical, Mechatronics, Mechanical, Aerospace, Systems or aviation related technical engineering discipline
  • 3-5 years experience in integration and test of hybrid powertrain or high voltage electric drive systems
  • Working knowledge of high voltage electric drive systems including motors/generators, inverters, and power electronics
  • Hands-on experience with powertrain dynamometer testing, motor characterization, or gearbox acceptance testing
  • Adept at working safely with high voltage systems (400V+), including integration, checkout, test, and safe discharge procedures
  • Strong test engineering foundation - DAQ setup and operation, sensor selection and installation, fluency in common communication protocols (CAN, Ethernet, Serial), and command line interface (CLI)
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, excellent verbal and written communication skills (effective for broad audiences)
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Defense Industry background desirable
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance in United States, United Kingdom, or Australi

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with hybrid-electric or full-electric propulsion systems in aerospace or UAS applications, particularly platforms where power-to-weight ratio and thermal constraints are critical design drivers.
  • Familiarity with battery management system (BMS) integration, battery module characterization, and safe handling of lithium-based energy storage systems in test environments.
  • Experience developing or operating Hardware In the Loop (HITL) or surrogate test platforms for powertrain control tuning and integrated system validation.
  • Exposure to rapid-iteration hardware development environments with short design-to-flight timelines, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and flight test support for prototype systems.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Inventory Control Coordinator, you will serve as the hands-on guardian of physical inventory accuracy across our warehouse operations. Working directly on the floor, you will execute daily cycle counts, investigate discrepancies between physical stock and system records, and drive root-cause corrective actions that prevent recurrence. This is a high-ownership, detail-driven role. You will not just count inventory—you will research transaction histories, trace process failures to their source, and prepare documented adjustment requests. The ideal candidate has sharp investigative instincts, thrives in a fast-paced environment, has a foundational understanding of aerospace/defense inventory compliance (including government property), and is passionate about physical inventory accuracy and continuous improvement.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own inventory accuracy, both physical and system records across all assigned locations.
  • Perform daily cycle counts, scheduled counts, and wall-to-wall physical inventories.
  • Investigate inventory discrepancies by researching transaction histories, receiving paperwork, and shipment documentation; trace variances from receipt through storage, picking, and shipment to pinpoint root cause.
  • Document the specific process failure of impactful variances, identify repeating failure patterns, and escalate systemic issues to IC leadership. Maintain RCCA records supporting AS9100 and government property compliance.
  • Reconcile physical inventory against WMS/ERP records and submit formal adjustment requests with complete supporting evidence; coordinate with IC Specialist and Supervisor to ensure timely review and approval.
  • Execute accurate inventory transactions—bin-to-bin movements, transfers, reservations, and unreservations—ensuring every movement is supported by the appropriate transfer order, work order, or documentation.
  • Maintain accurate bin locations, material master information, and clearly defined inventory locations. Identify and resolve misplaced, unidentified, excess, or damaged material with the responsible team.
  • Support material segregation and control for high-value, sensitive, or deployment-critical inventory.
  • Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and other material handling equipment.
  • Partner with Materials, Production, Deployment, and Supply Chain to develop inventory control procedures, standard work, and KPI reporting.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of experience in inventory control, warehousing, materials management, or a physical logistics role within an aerospace, defense, or high-volume hardware manufacturing environment.
  • Hands-on experience with cycle counting methodologies and physical inventory verification processes.
  • Proven ability to trace discrepancies to their root cause through documentation and transaction research.
  • Working proficiency with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) for inventory lookups and transaction review.
  • Analytical skills and proficiency working with Excel spreadsheets for sorting, filtering, and basic data analysis.
  • Ability to be onsite, local to Santa Ana, CA or Costa Mesa, CA

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Associate's degree in supply chain, manufacturing, business, or a related operations field.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, constantly changing environment with a high rate of production.
  • Experience working with digital inventory counting tools and barcode scanning environments.
  • Basic understanding of AS9100 standards, government property management guidelines, and 5S/Lean methodologies.
  • Experience with ABC inventory classification and Data Reconciliation counting programs.
  • Experience supporting process development and transitioning from low-volume/prototyping to high-rate production.
  • Strong investigative mindset and detail-oriented problem-solver who enjoys working as part of a high-performing, mission-driven warehouse team.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills to document findings clearly and collaborate across floor and office teams.

As a Lead Materials Coordinator, you will join our Deployment Operations team supporting one of Anduril's Test Sites. Test Sites are where our products meet the real world: dynamic, resource-constrained environments where rapid iteration, range operations, and customer demonstrations all happen. You will run with smaller teams and broader scope than production warehouses, which means the work is hands-on and the impact is immediate. The ideal candidate is an adaptable, proactive problem-solver who manages inventory and material operations under strict quality standards

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Process shipping, receiving, and inventory management at the Fort Stockton, TX test site
  • Coordinate and prepare inbound, outbound, and round-trip shipments moving between the test site, Anduril production facilities, and customer locations, including packaging, crating, labeling, and shipping documentation
  • Create and track shipment tickets in Jira, and coordinate delivery and pickup windows with carriers, drivers, and site security
  • Distribute received material to the correct team, lab, or individual on site, and track empty cases and non-inventory items back to their point of origin
  • Maintain inventory by identifying, labeling, and organizing materials and supplies, including bin locations and storage areas, and maintaining physical and digital records
  • Monitor inventory levels to identify anticipated material shortages and restock points, and raise them to site and Deployment Operations leadership
  • Pull, kit, pack, crate, label, and stage materials for test events, builds, and outbound shipments, ensuring product is properly secured and documented
  • Execute receiving, issuing, transfer order, and cycle-count transactions in Oracle and Odoo, including project striping and de-striping, and troubleshoot transfer order validation errors so material can move on schedule
  • Reconcile inventory records between systems when the physical count, Odoo, and Oracle disagree, escalating to Deployment Operations when a discrepancy cannot be resolved on site
  • Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and other machinery to move items, or signal machine operators to move materials onto and off trucks and loading docks
  • Transport material between the test site and nearby Anduril or partner locations as needed
  • Expedite flow of material, parts, and assemblies within the site and between Anduril locations in accordance with test and operational schedules

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10+ years as a materials coordinator, warehouse associate, or equivalent role
  • 2+ years of experience leading a team, training and mentoring employees for development
  • Knowledge of standard inventory management practices
  • Familiarity with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and/or other warehouse management and inventory control tooling
  • Ability to work proficiently and stay organized across multiple connected systems (ERP, Jira, Slack)
  • Ability to lift and move material, operate material handling equipment, and work on your feet in an active test environment
  • Ability to work onsite at the Test Site five days per week with occasional after-hours or weekend surge support as test and operational schedules dictate
  • Ability to travel to Anduril Headquarters in Costa Mesa, CA and other Anduril sites on occasion, no more than 20% travel
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years of forklift experience and license
  • Experience supporting field operations, test ranges, or remote / austere sites
  • Experience working in the defense/aerospace industry
  • Proficient with spreadsheets for inventory reconciliation, reporting, and ad-hoc analysis
  • Familiarity with inventory management through lot, serial, or batch tracking
  • Experience packaging and handling hazardous shipments
  • Able to operate independently and prioritize tasks effectively in fast-paced environments
  • Comfortable working directly with engineers and technicians in an active test environment
  • Excellent customer service skills
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. clearance

Anduril Industries is seeking a skilled and innovative Turbomachinery Manufacturing Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate will play a crucial role in developing and optimizing manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components used in our cutting-edge defense systems.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Design, develop, and implement robust, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components, from concept to production.
  • Specify, design, procure, and validate necessary tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing equipment to support production goals and process requirements.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure manufacturability of turbomachinery designs, including DFx principles.
  • Optimize existing manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.
  • Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, process flow diagrams, and quality control plans
  • Conduct root cause analysis for manufacturing defects, non-conformances, or process inefficiencies, and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
  • Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies and methodologies.
  • Ensure compliance with quality standards, safety regulations, and environmental requirements.
  • Manage projects related to turbomachinery manufacturing improvements and capacity expansion.
  • Provide technical support to production teams and train personnel on new processes and equipment.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in turbomachinery component manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or high-performance industrial gas turbine industries.
  • Experience with CAD/CAM software, preferably NX or similar.
  • Familiarity with CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and other advanced manufacturing technologies.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Experience integrating automation, robotics, or advanced metrology systems (e.g., CMM, optical scanning) into manufacturing workflows.
  • Owned end-to-end equipment development and implementation
  • Designing and fabricating tooling, such as mandrels and other fixture jigs

Anduril’s Manufacturing Technology, Maritime Team is seeking a Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Maritime Systems. The Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Manufacturing Planner, you will own the critical bridge between engineering design, supply chain, and shop-floor execution for our advanced autonomous systems. In this role, you will be responsible for defining the operational sequence of how we build hardware at scale. You will direct the creation and maintenance of detailed manufacturing plans, build and optimize MES routings, manage BOM structures, and ensure that technicians have clear, repeatable work instructions compliant with rigorous customer standards (including NAVSEA). You will play a pivotal role in turning broader functional plans into actionable processes, managing configuration changes, and maintaining production schedules within established timelines and budgets.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Manufacturing Planning & Execution: Direct the creation and maintenance of comprehensive manufacturing plans, oversee the translation of complex 2D/3D engineering drawings into clear work instructions, and optimize operational process routings in our MES.
  • Bill of Materials Management: Own the strategy for creation and maintenance of the MBOM and as-built configuration management, ensuring accurate translation from the EBOM.
  • Production Scheduling & Prioritization: Partner with Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain to establish build sequences, monitor order flow, and make sequencing and allocation decisions to support production ramp-up.
  • Engineering Change Coordination: Manage engineering changes across active manufacturing plans, assessing impact on active MES routings, work-in-progress, and hardware delivery timelines.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Serve as a primary interface between Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Production Operations to align on goals, resolve line blockers, and meet delivery commitments.
  • DFX Producibility Input: Collaborate upstream with design teams during DFM and DFA reviews to ensure assembly sequences, build procedures, and routings are optimized for cost, quality, and scalability.
  • Continuous Improvement: Analyze manufacturing discrepancies, scrap, and operational process data using first-principles problem-solving and root-cause analysis to enhance production efficiency and yield.
  • Shop-Floor Support: Provide hands-on manufacturing planning support directly on the floor during New Product Introduction (NPI), prototype builds, and rate ramp-ups.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of experience in manufacturing planning, production planning, or production control within a complex electromechanical or hardware manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated experience in a NPI environment, transitioning complex products from design into sustained, high-rate production.
  • Demonstrated expertise in creating and maintaining MBOMs, building process routings, and translating EBOM structures.
  • Hands-on experience with MES and Product Data Management (PDM) software.
  • Proficiency in reading and interpreting complex engineering drawings, technical specifications, and process maps.
  • Proven track record of navigating aggressive timelines, resource trade-offs, and prioritization decisions to support delivery commitments.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Direct experience in the maritime, naval, or aerospace defense industry, with an understanding of associated quality and documentation standards (e.g., NAVSEA, MIL-SPEC).
  • Hands-on experience with ERP systems (such as Oracle) for material and production planning.
  • Experience with CAD and PLM software (e.g., Siemens NX, Teamcenter) and issue-tracking platforms (e.g., JIRA).
  • Understanding of statistical process control (SPC), capacity planning, and lean manufacturing principles.

  • Passionately work across multiple programs from development to full rate production to scale best-in-class solutions to align with maturity of manufacturing process

ABOUT THE JOB

In this role, you will own the end-to-end mechanical development of novel, first-of-type Support Systems and Ground Servicing Equipment (GSE). You will take hardware from blank-sheet concept through detailed CAD, rapid prototyping, dynamic mechanism design, and production. Your scope spans launch and recovery systems, ruggedized expeditionary transport equipment, automated fueling and charging interfaces, and precision payload handling devices. WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Architect, model, and build novel Support Systems and Ground Servicing Equipment (GSE)—driving hardware from blank-sheet concept down-selection through CAD, physical prototyping, and fielded customer demonstrations.

  • Design and execute lean, right-sized test plans to validate new mechanisms, efficiently capturing empirical learnings to drive immediate CAD and hardware design revisions.
  • Design ruggedized systems tailored for austere land and dynamic maritime conditions, ensuring field survivability, high reliability, and intuitive human factors.

  • Establish and maintain baseline configuration control across fast-evolving prototype builds, test fixtures, and field-trial assets.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 3+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience owning the design, analysis, build, and functional test of complex physical hardware or mechanisms.
  • Strong foundation in first-principles mechanical design, structural packaging, material selection (metals, composites, hardware), and 3D CAD modeling.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with system safety practices, hazard assessments, and risk mitigation methodologies (e.g., MIL-STD-882E or equivalent industrial standards).
  • Hands-on mechanical aptitude with an iterative, prototype-to-learn mindset and a high bias for action in fast-paced environments.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience developing Ground Support Equipment (GSE), launch/recovery mechanisms, mobile heavy equipment, or transport and packaging solutions for aerospace or defense systems.
  • Operational experience in land or maritime expeditionary environments—supporting flight line operations, field maintenance, or complex tactical deployments.
  • Familiarity with high-voltage battery systems, electric powertrains, or fluid/fueling delivery systems.
  • Hands-on fabrication, trade, machining, or aircraft mechanic experience (A&P license or military maintenance MOS/AFSC).
  • Prior military service or defense contracting background with unmanned aerial systems (UAS).

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer to join the Maneuver Dominance team in our Costa Mesa office. The Maneuver Dominance (MD) Team at Anduril develops aerial robotic systems designed to operate in large coordinated teams in concert with ground maneuver forces.

Here you will work on core product development for unmanned rotorcraft and complex systems, including but not limited to design and development of a novel payload carriage and release system, analysis and testing of the system and it’s tooling design. The ideal candidate would be practical, hands-on and a self starter with high growth potential.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own and drive the physical design of the payload carriage and release for a novel aircraft type, overseeing the process from initial concept to low rate production.

  • Work in close partnership with other disciplines internal to Anduril to ensure the electrical, actuation, and mechanical systems collectively form a reliable, flexible, cost-effective system.
  • Spearhead design reviews, conduct analysis, build prototypes and design and implement hardware test plans.

  • BEng, BSc, MEng, MSc or higher in mechanical or aerospace engineering, or equivalent work experience.
  • 7+ years in a technical engineering role in a professional aerospace setting, with demonstrated track record of successful stakeholder management, consensus building and successful project delivery.
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter and strong proficiency in CAD software with specific emphasis on rapid concepting and iteration of novel designs.
  • Strong technical knowledge in core engineering principles, including fundamental mechanics of composite and metallic materials, design, analysis, testing, and fabrication.
  • Deep understanding of load paths, design practices, and hand calculations to design robust structurally efficient assemblies.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surfaces, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Metrology Specialist to join our rapidly growing team in Santa Ana, CA working in a cutting-edge production environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in maritime manufacturing. In this role, you will blend hands-on inspection with data-driven engineering analysis. You will be responsible for developing automated inspection routines for CMMs, creating alignment strategies for large- scale laser tracker measurements, and analyzing dimensional data to provide actionable feedback to the entire organization. Your work will support the full product lifecycle, from initial R&D and prototyping to process validation and full-rate production within our AS9100 certified system. This role requires a problem- solver's mindset and a passion for turning data into manufacturing improvement.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop, program, and execute inspection routines for CMMs using software like PC-DMIS or Polyworks.
  • Analyze inspection data to perform root cause analysis, support statistical process control (SPC) initiatives, and conduct capability studies.
  • Collaborate with Design and Manufacturing Engineers to provide Design for Manufacturability/Inspectability (DFM/DFI) feedback on new products.
  • Interpret complex engineering drawings and 3D CAD models to create comprehensive inspection plans that effectively validate GD&T requirements.
  • Generate clear and concise inspection reports and present findings to cross-functional teams to drive corrective actions.
  • Support the development and documentation of standard operating procedures for metrology processes within our AS9100 Quality Management System.
  • Assist in maintaining metrology equipment calibration and contribute to the selection of new measurement technology.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of experience in a manufacturing, quality, or metrology engineering role.
  • Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, a related engineering field, or equivalent experience.
  • Strong proficiency in interpreting and applying Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) per the ASME Y14.5 standard.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one major metrology software platform (PC-DMIS or Polyworks), with a strong aptitude to become proficient in others.
  • Experience working in a manufacturing environment governed by a formal Quality Management System (e.g., AS9100, ISO 9001).
  • Ability to read and interpret complex mechanical drawings and 3D CAD models.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.
  • Direct programming experience with multiple metrology platforms (e.g., proficiency in both PC-DMIS and Spatial Analyzer).
  • Hands-on experience with both fixed CMMs and portable metrology equipment (laser trackers, portable arms).
  • Experience creating First Article Inspection Reports (FAIRs) to the AS9102 standard.
  • Familiarity with CAD software (such as NX or SolidWorks) for interrogating models.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time sensitive, multi domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kills chains and enable mission autonomy. In Expeditionary Systems, we containerize warfighting functions. You will deploy our systems for missions in support of Homeland Defense.

The Mission Operations (MOPs) team is responsible for managing the execution, growth, and success of our customer accounts. Working across product, engineering, sales, and logistics teams, our Mission Operations Engineers own the customer relationships and develop, plan, and deploy Anduril products in support of their missions. They work side-by-side with customers to understand their specific problem sets and then shape Anduril’s offerings alongside our engineering teams to fit the mission needs. Because the problems we solve are uniquely challenging, our Mission Operations Engineers naturally gravitate toward finding solutions and are adept at navigating organizational hurdles. They are ultimately responsible for customer and mission success and therefore play a critical role in the shaping and future of Anduril Industries.

ABOUT THE JOB

Orchestrate the deployment of Anduril products. Lead the planning and deployment of Anduril’s flagship hardware and software products in support of customer missions. Through collaboration with our engineering, logistics, and technical operations teams, Mission Operators are in charge of deploying our products to the field, training end users, and ensuring the high performance of our products. We are obsessed about engagement and keeping our finger on the pulse of how customers interact with our products. This helps us improve the user experience and evolve their operational tactics and techniques. And if something isn’t quite right, we work with product teams to quickly address the issue on behalf of our customer.

Grow your business through customer success. In addition to the operational and executive relationships you own, you will be responsible for meeting commercial targets that drive top line growth. This requires establishing committed and trust-based partnerships with our customers to not only help them solve their immediate problems, but also to foresee future opportunities where Anduril’s technology can make them more effective. Understanding Anduril’s value proposition and articulating how we can have an impact on a customer’s problem set, from the executive level to the end user, is critical to positioning Anduril for the future.

Shape our products to meet mission needs. Work side-by-side with our customers to understand their specific mission challenges and represent the customer as you work with Anduril engineers to shape products that solve critical national and international security challenges. Anduril engineers rely on Mission Operators to understand the lay of the land and bring a perspective that informs the product development process.

Collaborate across nearly every Anduril team. Successfully deploying our complex hardware and software products requires collaborating with nearly every internal Anduril team - business development, engineering, product, logistics, finance, legal, contracting, technical operations, and many more. You’ll be responsible for ensuring each party is engaged and informed, and will therefore become well-versed in what it takes to really bring the best of Anduril to our customers.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Mission First Mindset. We put the needs of the mission and our customers first and understand that the US and its allies have no preordained right to victory in any future conflict. We actively seek out opportunities to better understand our customers’ mission needs, with a goal to build the best possible products for the warfighter and radically evolve our national and international defense capabilities. We push ourselves and the limits of our capabilities in the pursuit of this goal.

Ownership Mentality. We’re looking for owners; those who have a natural bias to assume responsibility, a healthy dose of skepticism, and contribute to a culture of performance. We empower our Mission Operators to quickly assume high levels of responsibility and entrust them to actively own their account and shape its success. Our Mission Operators are just as comfortable helping to shape a proposal or pitch a new customer as they are working with engineers on new features or deploying products in the field.

Technical Aptitude and Intellectual Curiosity. We are first and foremost a technology company, working at the leading edge of capabilities like machine learning, autonomy, distributed networking, and multi-modal sensor fusion. Do you have a natural desire to see beyond simple cause and effect relationships to really understand how complex systems operate? Do you actively seek out opportunities to educate yourself? These capabilities form the foundation of our product offerings, so we are looking for those who are comfortable communicating technical concepts and can articulate them in the context of the customer’s mission.

Structured Thinker and Problem Solver. Leading technical programs requires clear communication and well thought-out plans. We are looking for assertive communicators who bring a thoughtful perspective and honest dialogue. A solution-driven approach, the ability to distill complexity into its essential, digestible components, and the ability to supervise execution are critical to ensure mission success.

High Value Team Member. Do you enjoy working as part of a team? At Anduril, the path to success weaves through the organization - account teams, engineering, logistics, technical operations, and more. It requires humility, an eagerness to learn, and empathy toward your fellow team member. We assume best intentions and empathize with customers just as we do with our colleagues. Can you develop rapport at both the user and executive levels? Do you enjoy sharing successes? We are a low ego group that promotes teamwork and collaboration to bring about success.

360 Degree Leader. We are a flat, non-hierarchical organization with a matrix structure that is dynamic and evolving. We expect you to be self-aware enough to recognize your position of unstated leadership within the company. You should have a demonstrated ability to lead and influence people through both formal and informal constructs and in situations where there is lack of clarity across teams. Finally, we need people who identify gaps and breakdowns and solve them immediately, rather than point them out and step back. You should also seek 360 feedback to help inform your growth trajectory as a leader.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Serve in a customer-facing Account Manager capacity, working directly with a Department of War Service to develop and deploy Anduril integrated hardware-software C2 products to meet customer and operational needs. Manage the day-to-day customer engagement rhythm — meeting prep, action item follow-through, stakeholder map maintenance, and comms cadence with the customer’s team.
  • Own the delivery of contract deliverables to include the developing, and implementing, measures of performance and effectiveness, writing technical reports and creating user engagement roadmaps.
  • Design & implement user feedback loops to gather, triage, and prioritize requirements, feedback, issues, and challenges found through the employment of Anduril C2 products during training, exercises, and normal use within unit schedules.
  • Provide input to program and engineering teams to drive the development of product features and configurations that enhance or greatly improve efficiency of user workflows and employment of Anduril C2 products.
  • Develop and contribute to a streamlined user feedback and engagement system, which include issue tracking, training sessions, refreshers, and focused preparation for large scale exercises and events.
  • Own the working-level translation of customer requirements into engineering-actionable documentation. Maintain the requirements traceability matrix.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience in program management and product deployment roles
  • Exceptional interpersonal and stakeholder management skills
  • Understanding of U.S. and allied military operations, doctrines, and multi-domain environments
  • Experience translating and decomposing highly technical concepts into operational requirements and performance specifications
  • Strong aptitude for problem solving in unstructured situations at the interface of hardware, software, and networking. Ability to drive challenging and vague technical problems to clarity and resolution
  • Willing to travel as necessary (25-50%)
  • Secret Clearance or above required

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience in Defense Technology Product/Program Management or Solutions Architect type roles
  • Experience and familiarity with Homeland Defense, Ballistic Missile Defense, and/or dense compute work loads
  • Familiarity with doctrinal, functional, and technical command and control concepts, processes, and principles
  • Familiarity with Intelligence Community Directive 705 standards to support the physical security, construction, and accreditation of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs)

ABOUT THE JOB

You'll own spacecraft and payload structural analysis from conceptual design through environmental testing and launch.   • Identify and implement new scalable processes for demand, supply, and material planning

Anduril is seeking an experienced Power Controls Engineer to develop and implement advanced control algorithms for high-performance power electronic systems. We're looking for someone with deep expertise in control system modeling and simulation — particularly in Simulink and PLECS — who can take a controls concept from simulation through hardware validation. This individual will own the control architecture for DC/DC converters, inverters, and motor drives built around discrete SiC and GaN power stages, and will work closely with power hardware and firmware engineers to deliver tightly integrated, high-reliability systems for defense and aerospace applications.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Design, simulate, and validate closed-loop control algorithms for switch-mode power converters and inverters using Simulink and/or PLECS.
  • Controls for 3-phase AC systems, with and without a switched Neutral
  • Develop plant models and controller architectures (voltage-mode, current-mode, sensorless FOC, etc.) for multi-kW power stages utilizing discrete SiC and GaN FETs.
  • Perform stability analysis, loop shaping, and compensator design to meet transient response, efficiency, and EMI targets.
  • Collaborate with power hardware engineers on gate drive tuning, dead-time optimization, and switching-loss characterization of wide-bandgap devices.
  • Support model-based code generation workflows and work with firmware engineers to translate control designs into embedded implementations.
  • Define and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and power-hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) test plans to validate control performance against system requirements.
  • Contribute to trade studies on converter topology, modulation strategy, and control bandwidth as they relate to size, weight, power, and thermal constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or related discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience designing and tuning digital control loops for power electronic converters (DC/DC, DC/AC, or motor drives).
  • Proficiency in Simulink and/or PLECS for control system modeling, simulation, and analysis.
  • Strong foundation in control theory — z-domain and s-domain design, bode analysis, state-space methods, and discrete-time implementation considerations.
  • Hands-on experience with discrete SiC and/or GaN FET-based power stages in the multi-kW range.
  • Familiarity with military or aerospace environments and standards such as MIL-STD-461, 464, 810, or DO-160.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MS/PhD with a focus in power electronics controls or control systems.
  • Experience writing embedded firmware (C/C++) for microcontrollers or DSPs used in power converter control (e.g., TI C2000, STM32).
  • Familiarity with auto-code generation from Simulink (Embedded Coder) or similar model-based design toolchains.
  • Experience with real-time HIL platforms (e.g., Typhoon HIL, dSPACE, OPAL-RT).
  • Knowledge of advanced modulation techniques (SVM, DPWM) and their impact on switching losses in wide-bandgap devices.
  • Design-for-Reliability practices including DFMEA.
  • Experience with EMI mitigation strategies at the controls and layout level.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Product Support Engineer at Anduril, you will be a critical individual contributor within our rapidly growing Maritime team. You will drive the development and implementation of comprehensive sustainment strategies for cutting-edge defense products, directly contributing to their operational readiness and longevity. This is an impactful role where you will take ownership of defining critical maintenance plans, shaping technical data packages, optimizing sparing, and ensuring seamless lifecycle management. Your expertise will be vital in translating engineering innovation into reliable, supportable systems for our warfighters, directly enabling Anduril’s mission to transform defense technology. You will own product support analysis and sustainment cost for a fleet of maritime autonomous vehicles. Reporting to the Support System Lead, you will build the life cycle cost model, run the analysis that determines how the fleet gets supported, and turn reliability and maintenance data into the provisioning, manning, and cost picture the program and the customer need. Sustainment is where the majority of a platform's lifetime cost lands, and this role owns understanding it before those costs are locked in by design decisions.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop and maintain comprehensive, ground-up sustainment plans for the specific product(s) you support
  • Partner with customers, operations teams, and cross-functional engineering teams to define, implement, and continuously improve effective maintenance and repair strategies
  • Ensure the availability of up-to-date maintenance procedures, specialized tools, and accurate technical manuals to support field sustainment operations
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for all sustainment-related matters within your product team, proactively identifying and resolving issues
  • Collaborate with design and manufacturing engineering teams during new product development phases to integrate best sustainment practices and design-for-supportability concepts early in the process
  • Create and maintain a Service Bill of Materials (SBOM) and other critical sustainment artifacts (e.g., provisioning lists, support equipment lists), ensuring they establish a central, up-to-date repository for all sustainment data
  • Supply the support terms of the operational availability basis, meaning logistics delay and preventive maintenance time, alongside the reliability lead who owns the reliability allocations.
  • Build and maintain the life cycle cost estimate and the operating and support cost model, with sensitivity analysis and affordability reporting, and publish the estimate at program gates.
  • Build and own the life cycle cost model for the vehicle fleet and its support system.
  • Perform product support analysis covering provisioning, manning, facilities, and support equipment.
  • Produce operating and support (O&S) cost estimates and keep them current as the design matures.
  • Run cost trade studies on sustainment approaches and feed results into design decisions.
  • Develop spares and provisioning plans in partnership with RAM and Maintenance.
  • Define the product support strategy and supporting elements of the logistics architecture.
  • Produce cost and supportability analysis for customer deliverables and program reviews.
  • Establish the data pipeline that converts reliability and maintenance data into cost projections.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Logistics, Economics, Finance, or equivalent.
  • 5+ years of experience in product support, sustainment engineering, or systems engineering roles within a high-rigor environment (e.g., defense, aerospace, advanced robotics, complex industrial systems)
  • Demonstrated detailed and extensive technical expertise in applying mechanical or systems engineering principles to complex hardware systems
  • Experience building or maintaining a life cycle cost or operating and support (O&S) cost model and presenting its results to a program or customer audience.
  • Direct experience with sustainment methodologies such as Maintenance Task Analysis (MTA), Level of Repair Analysis (LORA), Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM), or developing Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) plans.
  • Foundational understanding and practical application of Integrated Product Support (IPS) elements, principles, and concepts (e.g., maintenance planning, supply support, technical data management, support equipment, training, facilities)
  • Familiarity with military standards, specifications, and regulatory compliance relevant to product support and sustainment activities
  • Proven ability to work effectively in dynamic, unstructured environments, adapt to rapidly changing priorities, and quickly learn and master new technologies and complex systems
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to synthesize complex technical and quantitative data into clear, concise decision statements and actionable recommendations for diverse audiences (engineers, operators, customers)
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Hands-on proficiency with professional CAD software and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools for managing engineering data, changes, and configurations
  • Proven track record of developing and delivering key customer-facing sustainment artifacts and contractual deliverables
  • Prior hands-on experience with specific enterprise tools such as Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), JIRA, or Oracle (ERP) or equivalent systems
  • Direct experience with complex military systems, robotics, unmanned systems, or advanced defense technology products
  • Understanding of the use of the Technical Data Package (drawings, parts lists, interface control documents, and electrical schematics)
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Willingness and ability to travel for on-site support, field deployments, and direct customer engagements as required
  • Experience with DoD product support analysis or Integrated Product Support elements.
  • Familiarity with LORA, provisioning analysis, and sparing optimization.
  • Background in naval or maritime sustainment cost.
  • Experience with performance-based logistics or sustainment contracting models.
  • Proficiency with cost modeling tools or scripting for analysis automation.

The Maritime Manufacturing Technology team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Quality Technician to join our rapidly growing team in Santa Ana, CA. The Quality Technician for our Maritime team is a critical role responsible for ensuring our autonomous surface and undersea systems are built to the most stringent standards, blending the speed and innovation of a technology company with the discipline and rigor required for national security.

You will be contributing to quality for programs that operate in the harshest environments on Earth. This role requires a hands-on, first-principles approach to developing and enforcing quality systems that meet and exceed AS9100 and specific Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) standards. You will not just be checking boxes; you will be building the quality foundation for the next generation of naval technology.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Support the Quality team to develop, implement, and sustain a robust Quality Management System (QMS) that is compliant with AS9100 and tailored to include specific NAVSEA requirements for maritime hardware.
  • Champion quality on the manufacturing floor. Support statistical process controls (SPC), conduct Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and continuous improvement initiatives to increase first-pass yield and reduce scrap.
  • Interpret and flow down NAVSEA standards and technical publications (e.g., material traceability, welding certifications, testing protocols) into actionable manufacturing and inspection processes.
  • Support the Material Review Board (MRB) to disposition non-conforming product. Help drive the Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) process using methodologies like 8D and 5 Whys to prevent recurrence.
  • Partner with the supply chain team to qualify, audit, and manage suppliers of critical components and special processes (e.g., welding, coatings, pressure testing), ensuring compliance with all prime contract and regulatory requirements.
  • Support the development of comprehensive inspection plans, work instructions, and criteria for receiving, in-process, and final inspection. Aid with First Article Inspections (FAIs) in accordance with AS9102.
  • Support internal and supplier audits to ensure system-wide compliance and identify opportunities for improvement. Support customer and third-party audits.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of experience in a Quality Engineering role within a manufacturing environment for aerospace, defense, or other regulated industries.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience implementing, maintaining, and being audited against an AS9100 certified Quality Management System.
  • Proficiency in root cause analysis methodologies (8D, 5 Whys, Fishbone, etc.) and implementing effective corrective actions.
  • Experience aiding First Article Inspections (FAIs) per AS9102.
  • Understanding of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) and the ability to interpret complex engineering drawings.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience with NAVSEA standards and requirements (e.g., SUBSAFE, NAVSEA S9074-AQ-GIB-010/248 for welding, material control specifications, technical publication adherence).
  • Experience in the production of maritime systems, including unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), or related pressure vessel and submersible hardware.
  • Experience with quality control for special processes such as composite fabrication, welding, complex electro-mechanical assembly, and environmental/pressure testing.
  • ASQ certification (Certified Quality Engineer - CQE, Certified Quality Auditor - CQA) or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt certification.
  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-mix, rapid development environment where speed and rigor must coexist.
  • Familiarity with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Manufacturing Execution System (MES) software.
  • Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own reliability, availability, and maintainability for a fleet of maritime autonomous vehicles. Reporting to the Support System Lead, you will set RAM requirements, run the predictive analysis that tells the program whether those requirements are achievable, and drive the design changes that close the gap. This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role spanning the entire product lifecycle - from early concept trade studies and detailed design through manufacturing scale-up, production, and sustained field performance. You'll be the reliability champion throughout the design and development process, working closely with mechanical, electrical, and software engineering teams to ensure designs are robust. You'll also partner with manufacturing, quality, test operations, and field service teams to transition these products from engineering prototypes to production-ready systems. Your scope will span performing predictive reliability analysis and FMEAs, developing and executing qualification and production test plans, leading root-cause failure investigations from both the factory floor and the field, and closing the loop to drive continuous design and process improvements. The right person for this role brings deep technical knowledge of hardware reliability and failure mechanisms, practical experience in both design and production environments, and the ability to drive cross-functional alignment without direct authority. This role demands an independent, data-driven engineer who can build reliability infrastructure from the ground up and take ownership of product performance from concept to deployment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support and review system block diagrams, interface control documents, and schematics for compliance, redundancy, and accuracy against requirements and concept of operations.
  • Lead Failure Modes & Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) efforts, collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams to implement design improvements.
  • Perform predictive reliability analysis to calculate probability of loss of control, loss of asset, and MTTF/MTBF utilizing Anduril requirements, specifications, and relevant industry standards (i.e. MIL-HDBK-217Plus).
  • Develop and execute comprehensive Qualification and Validation Test plans (including environmental, life/limit, and accelerated testing) to ensure appropriate requirements coverage and de-risking for production readiness; partner with Test Engineering to fixture and instrument test campaigns.
  • Work with Quality and Manufacturing Engineering to develop, refine, and validate assembly, integration, and testing processes (including inspection/acceptance test gates) to optimize build reliability and reduce time-to-deploy.
  • Develop Maintainability prediction models using MIL-HDBK-472, and support the development of Preventative Maintenance & Sparing plans.
  • Perform Weibull analysis utilizing data from qualification campaigns, production testing, and fielded assets to predict failures and identify trends.
  • Lead failure investigations on anomalies originating from design validation, production testing, and field returns; drive root cause analysis and corrective/preventative actions (CAPA) to closure.
  • Support Development Milestone Reviews through the identification of appropriate entry and exit criteria, guiding the transition of designs from engineering development to high-rate production.
  • Develop and implement standardized reliability processes, tools, and infrastructure to streamline and accelerate our design, manufacturing, and deployment operations.
  • Own RAM requirements definition, allocation, and verification across the vehicle and support system.
  • Build and maintain reliability models, predictions, and availability analysis for the fleet.
  • Lead FMECA, fault tree analysis, and criticality assessment across subsystems.
  • Drive design-for-reliability and design-for-maintainability requirements back into engineering.
  • Define the reliability growth program, including test-analyze-fix planning.
  • Establish failure reporting, analysis, and corrective action (FRACAS) and the data pipeline behind it.
  • Perform Level of Repair Analysis and maintainability modeling in partnership with Maintenance.
  • Set spares and provisioning inputs derived from reliability predictions.
  • Lead and mentor engineers across the RAM discipline as the function grows.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of 7+ years experience as a Reliability Engineer, Design/Development Engineer, Process Engineer, Automation Engineer, Industrial Engineer or Test Engineer
  • B.S. Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • Experience with safety-critical hardware & software systems in the defense or aerospace industry, with a preference for experience with Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
  • Experience or familiarity with MIL-STD-810, MIL-HDBK-217, MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-516C, and MIL-STD-1629
  • Experience setting up a Reliability Engineering framework for a product or program, including support of production testing, field testing, data acquisition, and data analysis
  • Expertise in reliability analysis techniques, including FMEA/FMECA, predictive modeling, Weibull analysis, and Fault Tree Analysis
  • Experience with generating qualification testing requirements and executing tests to proactively characterize product behavior and performance
  • Failure investigation/analysis experience with proven track record of solving problems and preventing reoccurrence
  • Design Review Experience (PDR, CDR, MRR) and confidence in presentation skills across all levels of leadership
  • Eligibility to obtain/maintain a U.S. Secret clearance, as required
  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Reliability Engineering, or equivalent.
  • 7+ years in reliability, RAM, or sustainment engineering on complex electromechanical systems.
  • Demonstrated ownership of RAM requirements and predictions on a program.
  • Hands-on experience with FMECA, fault tree analysis, and reliability modeling.

Anduril’s Research Scientists excel at developing state-of-the art algorithms and software that solve scientific problems with real-world applications.
